liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Playing in the Band** (5 reviews): The Playin' > El Paso > Playin' > Wharf Rat > Playin' > Morning Dew sandwich is called among the Dead's finest work; Reviewer finds the second-set Playin' sequence loose yet tight, and special among the many Playin' sequences over the years [7][8][9][14][17]
- **Here Comes Sunshine** (2 reviews): Here Comes Sunshine is singled out for energetic playing early in the show; Here Comes Sunshine in the first set is the one standout that really impresses this reviewer [7][9]
- **Mexicali Blues** (1 review): Garcia plays a Mexican Hat Dance for about forty seconds before Weir counts off Mexicali Blues [11]
- **They Love Each Other** (1 review): They Love Each Other has an early-'73 lilt, slightly jauntier than other versions [11]
- **Big River** (1 review): Big River rips [17]
- **El Paso** (1 review): El Paso seemed a little out of place in the Playin' sandwich [15]
- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Let It Grow is praised as well jammed and a highlight of the first set [7]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): The Truckin' into the closing stretch falls a bit flat [16]

## Setlist highlights

- **Nobody's Fault Jam**: rare: 13 archived performances [19]

## The recordings

- **gd73-11-21.sbd.barrick.192.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 27 songs; 177 min; rated 4.68/5 by 22 [1]. Said about its sound: B. Yerys reports digital glitches on disc 1 track 1, around 0:42; Reviewer hears tuning problems and missed notes, suggesting a somewhat off night for the band; Reviewer finds the sound perfect [1][10][14][15]
- **gd73-11-21.sbd-patched.warner.22097.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 28 songs; 178 min; rated 4.75/5 by 4 [2]
- **gd1973-11-21.sbd.miller.88612.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 25 songs; 183 min; rated 4.65/5 by 20 [3]. Said about its sound: Flaws and noises were cleaned up, and pitch was corrected by minus 2.7 percent with Cool Edit Pro [3]
- **gd1973-11-21.sbd.fix.miller.97468.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 26 songs; 183 min; rated 4.47/5 by 19 [4]

## Around the show

- A Mexican Hat Dance tuning bit follows Big Railroad Blues [3]
- Reviewer is a Denver native, so this hometown show holds special charm for them [8]
- Dire Wolf and Black Throated Wind appear in neither Deadbase V nor Deadbase X setlists [11]
- Reviewer hears Morning Dew as about average for its era [9]
- The show has the flow and consistency found in nearly all '73 shows [12]
- Reviewer wishes the third disc had the Truckin' jam from 11/20 instead [16]
- The Dew is very solid but not quite at the level of 6/18/74 or 5/8/77 [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd73-11-21.sbd.barrick.192.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Source credited to D. Barrick (hurtsme2) for this soundboard transfer [1]
- **gd73-11-21.sbd-patched.warner.22097.sbeok.shnf**: source: MSR > DAT > CD > Samsung SW-232B extraction (EAC v0.95 prebeta 4) > CDWave v1.71 (tracking) > sector boundary verification (shntool v1.01) > .shn encoding… [2]. Also: This is a patched soundboard source [16]
- **gd1973-11-21.sbd.miller.88612.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD D [3]. Also: Gaps are filled from a Sony stereo mic master cassette, via CD, in Goin' Down the Road and other spots [3]
- **gd1973-11-21.sbd.fix.miller.97468.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD [4]
